name: New ERA of Wrestling World Heavyweight Championship
notes: Jean Rabesque was billed champion by January 2005; the Phantom Republican's own reign, begun around 12 January 2006, is now structured (see reigns) and independently corroborated by an 18 April 2006 cross-federation posting naming him champion and Jean Rabesque his immediate predecessor. A co-championship split with Rocko Daymon by mid-2009 after a merger with WFW is attested only by billing on cards served elsewhere in the held record. New ERA's own rules document, dated 15 January 2011 in its own text, states that when the federation switched to a season-based format its reigning World Heavyweight Champion "became" the first champion of a renamed New ERA Championship -- the same title continuing under a new name, not a new belt -- and eliminated the Television and PRODIGY Classic Xtreme Championships, folding their own champions into the new title's bankable-shot system. The corpus does not capture who held the belt at that exact transition, though its own next captured card already bills a champion (see reigns r004) who names, in his own promo, the rival he took the belt from. The title changed hands at least three more times across 2011 (see reigns r004-r007), with a final open challenge left unresolved when the held record's last captured card ends without a results document.
epitaph: New ERA of Wrestling's own top championship, first crowned in a Fatal Fourway Battle Royal at the federation's founding show, carried through a 2009 merger and unification with a second promotion's own world title, and renamed the New ERA Championship when the federation switched to a season-based format in 2011 -- the held record's last captured card, in 2015, still finds it standing at the center of an unresolved open challenge.

name: New ERA of Wrestling Television Championship
notes: MWG is billed champion by the federation's own 17 September 2005 RAPTURE card, defending against Mr. Entertainment; the immediately preceding International Intrigue pay-per-view (9 June 2005) put him against the title's own prior #1 contender, Jason Payne, with no titleholder marked on either man, suggesting the title changed hands at that show, though no results document confirms it directly. A later champion, Cameron Cruise, is billed against Erik Black on the federation's own Destrucity II card (23 January 2010), more than four years later, with nothing in the held record's text bridging the two reigns; recorded as an honest gap rather than a guessed chain.
epitaph: New ERA of Wrestling's second-tier singles title, contested across the federation's whole run from an ambiguous 2005 change through a merger-era reign four years later, with no results document ever confirming a change of hands directly.

name: New ERA of Wrestling World Tag Team Championship
notes: Attested only by a single card's own billing (WFW:NE's Destrucity II, 23 January 2010): Cameron Cruise and Problem Child are named champions, defending against Jack n' Hoff. No earlier title history or results document survives in this corpus's own read slice.
epitaph: New ERA of Wrestling's tag title, attested only once in the held record, at a 2010 pay-per-view defense by Cameron Cruise and Problem Child.

name: New ERA PRODIGY Classic Xtreme Championship
notes: First seen contested at a tournament final on the federation's own International Intrigue pay-per-view (9 June 2005, Chaos vs. Dallas Carter), with no result recorded. Jason Payne is billed champion on two 2009 cards, the Almost Live special (26 June) and Unplugged (18 July); nothing in the held record's text connects his reign back to the 2005 tournament. The title is vacated and recontested in a new single-night tournament on the federation's own Destrucity II card (23 January 2010, John Doe, Ashe Corvin, Trevor Cane and Chaos), again with no result recorded; recorded as an honest gap rather than a guessed chain throughout.
epitaph: A cross-promotional hardcore title, crowned and re-crowned across the federation's own run in tournaments whose own outcomes this corpus never directly records.

name: New ERA of Wrestling Women's Heavyweight Championship
epitaph: The one championship of New ERA of Wrestling's women's division, won by Karla Starr at the first BattleBRAWL in December 2004 and held by her for two years until Juliet Marceau announced it over on RAUCOUS of 19 December 2006 and Starr took off its faceplate to reveal the VENUS World Heavyweight Championship underneath.
